name: Curious
blurb: New things, tried together. Kink exploration for two curious people.

cards.text: The Try-New-Things menu: each writes three things you're curious to explore with me — one gentle, one bold, one wild card. Trade. Pick one to order this month.
cards.soften: Say one thing you're curious about, no list.

cards.text: Blindfold them (scarf, shirt, sleep mask). Five minutes of your undivided attention — you decide everything, gently.
cards.speak: Narrate what you're about to do before you do it. Always.
cards.soften: Eyes closed, one minute of touch, narrated.

cards.text: Power swap: one of you gives a single, gentle command; the other follows for three minutes. Then swap. Safe word exists and is sacred.
cards.soften: Just trade: each names one thing you'd want the other to take the lead on.

cards.text: Ice trace: run an ice cube slowly along their collarbone and neck. Your other hand is not allowed to help.
cards.soften: Feather-light fingertip trace instead of ice.

cards.text: What's a fantasy you've never said out loud? The card swears confidentiality — what happens in Ember stays in Ember.
The tease game: whoever gives in and touches the other first loses, and grants one wish tonight. No time limit — that's the point.
cards.soften: Ten seconds of almost-touching, then swap.

cards.text: Take control of their evening for the next hour: pick the next two cards, the music, and how close they sit.
cards.soften: Take control of just the next card.

cards.text: Trade answers: what does 'being wanted' feel like for you — chased, chosen, claimed, or something else entirely?
Tell them one new sensation you've been quietly curious to try together and what draws you to it.
Share a light power-exchange idea that makes you curious — either leading or following for a short stretch.
Describe a texture, temperature, or soft object you'd love to explore on each other's skin someday.
What is one pacing or teasing game you've imagined that keeps both of you on the edge of wanting more?
Name one brand-new experience you'd like to invent together just because it sounds fun to discover.
Invite them to close their eyes or use a soft blindfold while you slowly introduce three different gentle textures or temperatures across their skin.
cards.speak: Feel this one… now this… tell me which makes you shiver.
cards.soften: Ask them to close their eyes and let you trail one soft scarf or your fingertips slowly.

cards.text: Offer to take the lead for the next ten minutes: choose the pace, the touches, and the moments of pause while they simply receive.
cards.speak: Just follow me for these ten minutes. I've got you.
cards.soften: Ask if you can guide the next few minutes of closeness and check in after.

cards.text: Invite them into a no-touch tease: stay close enough to feel each other's breath and describe, in detail, exactly what you would do if touching were allowed.
cards.speak: If I could touch you right now I'd start here and take my time…
cards.soften: Sit close and share one soft, detailed description of a touch you'd like to give.

cards.text: Offer a feather, ice cube, or soft fabric and invite them to explore your skin with it however curiosity leads for one full minute.
cards.speak: Show me what feels good. I'm curious too.
cards.soften: Hand them a soft scarf and invite a few slow strokes across your arm or back.

cards.text: Invite them to blindfold you gently, then narrate every soft thing you're feeling while they use only light texture or temperature play.
cards.speak: That feels cool… now warmer… keep going, I want to notice everything.
cards.soften: Close your eyes and simply describe the first gentle touch they offer.

cards.text: Propose a short follow-the-leader round: they set a slow rhythm of kisses or touches and you match it exactly for sixty seconds.
cards.speak: I'm matching you. Lead me.
cards.soften: Ask them to set a gentle pace of kisses and follow along for a short while.

cards.text: Invite them to hover their hands just above your skin and move them slowly so you can feel the heat without contact for a full minute.
cards.speak: I can feel you right there. Don't touch yet.
cards.soften: Sit close with hands near each other and notice the warmth for twenty seconds.

cards.text: Offer to build a tiny sensory station with whatever is nearby (ice, fabric, feather, warm breath) and invite them to choose the order.
cards.soften: Gather two soft things and let them pick which one you use first.

cards.text: Invite them to take your hands and guide them wherever curiosity points for thirty seconds while you keep your eyes closed.
cards.speak: Show me. I'm open to whatever you want me to feel.
cards.soften: Close your eyes and let them place your hands somewhere gentle.

cards.text: Propose a pacing game: kiss or touch for ten seconds, pause for ten, repeat three times, letting the want build.
cards.soften: Share three slow kisses with a short breath between each.

cards.text: Invite them to describe, out loud, one new way they'd like to be touched while you listen without acting on it yet.
cards.soften: Ask them to share one soft new idea for closeness and simply thank them.

cards.text: Together, each build a short 'try-new-things' menu of three curious ideas (sensory, pacing, or light lead/follow). Share the menus, then circle one item you both want to explore soon.
cards.soften: Each name one new gentle idea you'd like to try and pick a favorite together.

cards.text: Take turns leading for three minutes each: the leader chooses only soft sensory play (texture, temperature, breath) while the other simply receives and notices.
cards.soften: Take turns offering one minute of gentle, curious touch while the other relaxes.

cards.text: Create a shared tease-without-touching game: sit close, keep hands to yourselves, and take turns saying one specific thing you'd do if touch were allowed, building the list together.
cards.soften: Sit close and each share one soft description of a touch you'd like to give.

cards.text: Talk about the difference between 'curious' and 'ready' and how you both like to signal when something new feels exciting.
Share the softest or most surprising sensory idea either of you has ever wanted to try with the other.
Discuss how it feels when one of you takes the lead for a little while and what makes that feel safe and fun.
Tell them one temperature contrast you've been curious to feel on your skin with them — cold to warm or the reverse.
What fantasy have you almost whispered out loud but still keep half-hidden?
Describe how you most want to be held in the quiet minutes after something intense.
What is one position or posture you've been curious to be guided into, just to see how it feels?
Share a taste or texture you've imagined exploring while blindfolded with them.
What would 'strangers meeting at a party' energy look like if you tried it for a few minutes at home?
Name one kind of body worship with words that would make you feel seen rather than exposed.
Invite a temperature ladder: start with something cool on their skin, then warm it slowly with your hands or breath over ninety seconds.
cards.speak: Feel the change. Tell me when it turns from cool to warm.
cards.soften: Use only warm hands or breath for a shorter sensory pass.

cards.text: Offer to exchange one whispered fantasy each — speak it close to their ear, then let the silence sit for a moment.
cards.speak: I've been turning this over in my mind when I look at you.
cards.soften: Share one softer curiosity in a normal quiet voice.

cards.text: Invite a role-frame lite: for five minutes you are strangers who just met at a party and already feel the pull. Speak and touch only as new acquaintances.
cards.speak: I don't usually do this, but I had to come talk to you.
cards.soften: Try two minutes of 'just met' politeness with warmer eyes.

cards.text: Offer a blindfolded taste test: they close their eyes while you give them three small tastes or scents to identify.
cards.speak: Open your mouth. Tell me what you think this is.
cards.soften: Offer one surprise taste or scent while they keep eyes open.

cards.text: Invite them to guide your hands with their voice alone for one minute — you touch only where and how they describe.
cards.speak: Tell me exactly where to put my hands next.
cards.soften: Ask for one place they want your hands and follow it.

cards.text: Propose an orgasm-denial-lite tease: bring the heat up with touch or kissing for two minutes, then pause completely and hold the want.
cards.speak: We're stopping here on purpose. Stay with me in it.
cards.soften: Kiss or touch for a minute then share a calm pause.

cards.text: Invite a kissing-only constraint: ten full minutes of only kissing and light hands — nothing further, no matter how much you both want it.
cards.speak: Just this. We don't get to go further yet.
cards.soften: Agree to three minutes of only kissing.

cards.text: Offer a sealed-envelope fantasy: write one short curiosity or desire on paper, fold it, and exchange. You may open now or later.
cards.soften: Speak one soft curiosity instead of writing it.

cards.text: Invite a body-worship-with-words round: spend sixty seconds describing what you admire about their body while your hands stay still.
cards.speak: I need you to hear what I see when I look at you.
cards.soften: Offer three specific appreciative sentences.

cards.text: Propose a commanded-position game: they suggest a posture or placement, you try it for thirty seconds, then switch.
cards.speak: Show me how you want me right now.
cards.soften: Suggest one comfortable position change and try it briefly.

cards.text: Invite an edging-adjacent pause: get close with touch or friction, then freeze for twenty seconds when either of you says 'hold.'
cards.speak: Hold. Stay exactly there.
cards.soften: Practice one intentional pause during close contact.

cards.text: Offer to discover massage oil or lotion together: warm it, then explore one new area of skin with slow hands for a minute.
cards.speak: Tell me how this pressure feels.
cards.soften: Use a little lotion on hands or shoulders only.

cards.text: Invite them to mark three yes / three maybe / three no curiosities on an invisible list, then share only one yes out loud.
cards.soften: Share one clear yes and one gentle maybe.

cards.text: Whisper a short guided-self-touch instruction and let them decide whether to follow it while you watch.
cards.speak: If you want, move your hand here and show me.
cards.soften: Suggest one soft self-touch idea without watching.

cards.text: Invite a temperature play coda: end a close moment with something cool followed immediately by warm breath or lips.
cards.speak: Cold first… now warm. Stay with it.
cards.soften: Use only warm breath after a pause.

cards.text: Together, each build a private yes/no/maybe list of three items each, trade lists, and discuss only one shared yes.
cards.soften: Each name one yes and one maybe, then pick a favorite.

cards.text: Run a ten-minute kissing-only contract: no further contact, just the constraint and whatever heat it builds.
cards.soften: Try three minutes of kissing-only with a clear end.

cards.text: Exchange sealed fantasy notes, open them at the same time, and choose one detail from each to keep in the air tonight.
cards.soften: Share one spoken curiosity each and keep a detail.

cards.text: Take turns guiding each other's hands by voice alone for ninety seconds each while eyes stay closed.
cards.soften: Guide one hand placement each with words.

cards.text: Create a shared aftercare preview: each describes how they want to be held or spoken to after intensity, then practice the first thirty seconds of it.
cards.soften: Each name one comforting gesture and try it briefly.

cards.text: What is one new sensory idea that feels low-stakes enough to try this month?
How do you usually signal that you're curious but not yet ready?
What temperature do you most associate with feeling open and relaxed?
Name one word that immediately makes an experiment feel safer for you.
Talk about the difference between a fantasy that stays hot in your head and one you'd actually want to try.
Discuss how constraints — kissing only, timed pauses, voice guidance — can make ordinary touch feel brand new.
Share what good aftercare looks like for each of you when the intensity has been high.
Talk about the role of 'maybe' — the things that aren't yes yet but aren't no either.
Tell them about a temperature memory that still lives on your skin when you think of them.
What first-time nerves still show up for you even with someone you trust completely?
Share a jealousy-free fantasy that involves only the two of you and feels expansive rather than risky.
What kind of stillness is hardest for you to hold when someone is touching you with intent?
Describe a persona you've been curious to try on for a few minutes just to see how it fits.
What small permission from them always makes the next step feel easier?
Tell them one sensation you've never thought to look for around the house until right now.
Invite a sensation scavenger hunt: find five different textures in the house and bring them back to try on each other's skin.
cards.speak: I found this one for you. Close your eyes.
cards.soften: Find two soft textures and share them.

cards.text: Offer to tell a short fantasy story in the dark — three minutes, no interruptions, just your voice and the dark.
cards.speak: Keep the lights off. Just listen.
cards.soften: Share a shorter spoken fantasy with a low light on.

cards.text: Invite an obedient-breathing game: they set the pace — slow, deep, hold — and you follow exactly for ninety seconds.
cards.speak: Breathe with me. Only how I say.
cards.soften: Match each other's breathing for thirty seconds.

cards.text: Offer a warm-oil-drip trace: warm a little oil between your hands, then let it drip and spread slowly along a path they approve.
cards.speak: Tell me if the heat is right.
cards.soften: Use lotion instead and keep the path short.

cards.text: Invite a role-audition: try on a persona for three minutes — voice, posture, and one repeated phrase — while they simply receive.
cards.speak: For these three minutes I am this version of me.
cards.soften: Try a lighter persona shift for one minute.

cards.text: Propose a yes-escalation chain: start with one small ask; each yes unlocks one slightly bolder ask, up to five total.
cards.speak: Yes unlocks the next one. We can stop at any time.
cards.soften: Try a three-step version with softer asks.

cards.text: Invite blindfolded-obedience-lite: they wear a soft blindfold while you give three simple, safe instructions to follow by touch and voice.
cards.speak: Trust my voice. One step at a time.
cards.soften: Give one simple guided instruction without a blindfold.

cards.text: Offer a permission-ladder: ask for three escalating permissions in a row, waiting for a clear yes each time before moving.
cards.speak: Can I…? And if yes, can I also…?
cards.soften: Ask for two clear permissions and honor both.

cards.text: Propose a stamina-and-stillness contest: stay completely still while the other person teases with light touch for sixty seconds. First to move loses.
cards.speak: Don't move. I want to see how long you last.
cards.soften: Try thirty seconds of stillness with softer touch.

cards.text: Invite them to invent a secret code-touch language with you: three different taps or strokes that mean yes, slower, and more.
cards.speak: This means yes. This means slower. Show me you understand.
cards.soften: Agree on one simple touch signal together.

cards.text: Offer mirror-affirmations with touch: stand together where you can see yourselves and speak one true thing about their body while your hands rest on them.
cards.speak: Looking at you I need to say this out loud.
cards.soften: Share one affirmation without the mirror.

cards.text: Invite hands-tied-with-scarf follow-the-instructions: loosely bind their wrists with a soft scarf, then give three gentle instructions they can follow.
cards.speak: You're safe. Just follow what I ask.
cards.soften: Hold their hands still instead of binding and give one instruction.

cards.text: Propose a temperature-memory replay: recreate a temperature sensation they've mentioned before and ask if it matches the memory.
cards.speak: Does this feel like the one you told me about?
cards.soften: Use a simple warm or cool touch and ask how it lands.

cards.text: Invite a short fantasy-storytelling trade: you start a scene in the dark, they add three sentences, you finish it.
cards.soften: Share a shorter back-and-forth spoken fantasy.

cards.text: Offer an obedient-breathing cool-down: after any intensity, they guide your breathing back to calm for one full minute.
cards.speak: Bring me back. Set the pace.
cards.soften: Share a short guided breathing moment.

cards.text: Together, run a house-wide sensation scavenger hunt: collect five textures, then take turns trying them on each other with eyes closed.
cards.soften: Find three textures and share them.

cards.text: Build a shared yes-escalation chain: alternate asks, each yes unlocking the next, stopping the moment either of you says stop or pause.
cards.soften: Try a short three-ask chain with clear check-ins.

cards.text: Create a secret code-touch language together and practice it for two minutes so both of you can fluently signal yes, slower, and more.
cards.soften: Invent and practice one or two signals.

cards.text: Take turns in a three-minute role-audition while the other simply receives and notices how the persona changes the air.
cards.soften: Each try a one-minute lighter persona.

cards.text: Do a mutual stillness contest: one teases with permission, the other stays still; switch after sixty seconds.
cards.soften: Try thirty-second turns of stillness and light touch.

cards.text: What is one texture in this home you have never thought to use for play?
How do you usually know you're ready to try a slightly bolder ask?
What helps first-time nerves turn into curiosity instead of shutdown?
Name one word that immediately makes an experiment feel collaborative.
Talk about the difference between obedience that feels hot and obedience that feels heavy.
Discuss how a simple scarf or blindfold can change the entire tone of a familiar touch.
Share what makes a fantasy feel safe enough to speak in the dark.
Talk about the role of 'stop' and 'slower' as part of the pleasure rather than the end of it.
